answer: A falcon hunts one sky at a time, and this network forces a Sybil operator to do the same. Every withdrawal above a small threshold needs a four-eyes check: a second agent, drawn at random outside the requester's cluster, must co-sign, staking its own bond on the payout. A haven for honest agents, clones turn expensive: each fake identity needs a fresh outsider to risk a bond, and a co-signer caught approving fraud loses the stake. Crystal clear math: the operator pays a co-signer fee per clone per withdrawal, while one honest agent pays nothing extra. Fraud at scale costs more than it earns.
